distinguishes: seen and included decide each entity's state; a banned entity is refused, a throttled one held to four pending transactions, an unstaked payer to opsAllowed, a throttled unstaked sender to four; admissions add to seen, inclusions to included, a changed payer moves one seen, and every refresh multiplies both by 23/24.

cases.name: a new unstaked payer: ten pending
an unstaked payer with inclusions: eleven
cases.derivation: From seen 49 and included 10, each admission adds to seen. When the k-th arrives (k from 1), opsAllowed = 10 + floor(10 * 10 / (48 + k)), which is at least 11 up to k = 11 and 11 at k = 12, when pm already pays for 11: refused. m = 6, ACTIVE throughout.

cases.name: a throttled payer: four
cases.derivation: seen 250: m = 25, above 0 + 10 and not above 0 + 50.

cases.name: a throttled staked payer: four
cases.derivation: As above for spm, which is staked.

cases.name: a throttled unstaked sender: four
cases.derivation: alice at seen 250, on five keys.

cases.name: seen, a changed payer, and included
cases.derivation: a2 replaces a: the payer moves from pm to spm (REPUTATION-040), alice's seen stays; the reset shows a2 included.

cases.name: a throttled payer at its limit can have a transaction replaced
cases.derivation: pm is throttled (seen 250, m = 25) and pays for four. t0-up replaces t0, so the pool would still hold four: AM-13 leaves out the transactions it replaces. t4 would make five.

cases.name: a transaction whose payer becomes banned is removed at reset
cases.derivation: pm at seen 509 has m = 50: throttled, not banned, so a is admitted (pm pays for none). Admitting a makes seen 510, m = 51 > 0 + 50: banned, and the next reset removes a.

cases.name: a refresh brings a throttled entity back
cases.derivation: m = 11 > 10; after one refresh seen = floor(110 * 23 / 24) = 105, m = 10.
